anomalies.observed: On the MCU sheet the heater high-side switch U4 (TPS1H200AQDGNRQ1) has pin 1 (IN) on net NET0002 and pin 2 (DIAG_EN) on a different net NET0001. NET0002 is the ESP32 GPIO1/HEATER net (U3 pin 13) and the heater status-LED path (J6/D8/R6). NET0001 is, however, also the chip-select net of thermocouple U6 (MAX31855KASA pin 6, Thermocouples sheet). So the heater switch's DIAG_EN is merged onto a thermocouple SPI chip-select line instead of being tied to IN/GPIO1.
anomalies.expected: The specification states the heater switch is 'driven by ESP32 GPIO1 on both IN and DIAG_EN' and 'IN/DIAG_EN (pins 1/2) are both driven from ESP32 GPIO1 (net /Microcontroller/HEATER)'. Pins 1 and 2 must share the HEATER/GPIO1 net, and each thermocouple CS net must connect only to its own MAX31855 CS pin and its MCU GPIO, not to the heater switch.

anomalies.impact: The smart high-side switch's diagnostic-enable input is driven by a thermocouple chip-select line rather than held with the heater drive. During sequential thermocouple polling, DIAG_EN toggles with U6's CS, so the TPS1H200's diagnostic/FAULT reporting is coupled to thermocouple selection instead of to the heater control signal — a deviation from the intended wiring that changes the heater switch's fault-reporting behaviour.

parsed.summary: The schematic matches the specification on power rails, the power mux, the buck regulator, the thermocouple SPI topology (shared SCK/SO, three independent CS) and the heater switch's VS/CL/FAULT/OUT/GND pins, but the heater switch's DIAG_EN (U4 pin 2) is wired onto a thermocouple chip-select net (NET0001, shared with U6 pin 6) instead of being tied to the IN/HEATER net (NET0002) as the spec requires — a bridged-nets anomaly.
